docs.title: About me
docs.text:
I am a Biochemistry graduate from the University of Leeds, currently studying MSc AI in Bioscience at Queen Mary University of London. I am developing skills in programming, bioinformatics and biological data analysis, building on my scientific background.

My interests include molecular biology, pharmacology and how computational methods can support biological research. Alongside my studies, hospitality work, sports coaching and rugby captaincy have developed my teamwork, communication and ability to work under pressure.

docs.title: Academic project
docs.text:
Monoclonal antibody aggregation - undergraduate literature review

My final-year dissertation examined the biochemical causes of monoclonal antibody aggregation, its implications for therapeutic development and manufacturing, and approaches to reducing aggregation. This developed my ability to evaluate research evidence, synthesise findings and communicate scientific ideas clearly.

docs.text:
• Scientific research: Evaluated and brought together published findings through my dissertation and academic study.
  • Laboratory work: Developed practical scientific skills and an understanding of experimental design through undergraduate laboratory training.
  • Programming and data analysis: Used Python, Jupyter, pandas and Matplotlib in scientific programming exercises and a group dashboard project.
  • Bioinformatics: Applied Linux workflows to biological sequence processing, genome assembly and variant analysis.
  • Version control and documentation: Used Git, GitHub, Markdown and MkDocs to track changes, document work and maintain this portfolio.

docs.title: Introduction and overview
docs.text:
Developed practical Python skills for biological data analysis, progressing from core programming concepts to sequence analysis, AI-assisted coding and interactive data visualisation.

The module combined Jupyter notebook exercises with bioinformatics applications and a group hackathon, applying programming skills to biological sequences and public-health data.

docs.title: Skills developed
docs.text:
• Programming: Python, reusable code, object-oriented design, debugging and testing.
  • Data analysis: API access, JSON, pandas, data preparation and interactive visualisation.
  • Bioinformatics and AI: Biological sequence processing and critical evaluation of AI-generated code.
  • Version control: Managed project history, reviewed changes and resolved conflicts using Git and GitHub.
  • Teamwork and communication: Collaborative problem-solving, developing a shared application and explaining technical work.

docs.title: 1. First steps in Python
docs.text:
• Wrote and ran Python code using variables, data types, arithmetic and user input.
  • Manipulated strings, including simple DNA and RNA sequence examples.

docs.title: 2. Collections
docs.text: • Used lists, tuples and dictionaries to organise biological data, with indexing, slicing and comprehensions.

docs.title: 3. Conditional statements
docs.text: • Applied Boolean logic and if/elif/else statements to make decisions and filter data.

docs.title: 4. Iterative constructs
docs.text: • Used for and while loops, zip, break and continue to automate repetitive calculations and sequence processing.

docs.title: 5. Working with files
docs.text: • Read, parsed and wrote FASTA and CSV files, using context managers to handle files reliably.

docs.title: 6. Functions
docs.text: • Wrote reusable functions with arguments, return values and docstrings, applying them to biological sequence processing.

docs.title: 7. Modules
docs.text: • Organised code into reusable modules, worked with imports and namespaces, and included standalone test code.

docs.title: 8. Object-oriented programming and error handling
docs.text:
• Created classes with attributes and methods, and explored inheritance and polymorphism.
  • Used exception handling and custom exceptions to manage invalid input and runtime errors.

docs.title: 9. Biopython
docs.text:
• Used sequence objects for reverse complementation, transcription and translation.
  • Read FASTA and GenBank records with SeqIO and explored BLAST search results with SearchIO.

docs.title: 10. Git and GitHub
docs.text:
• Managed an example RNA-seq metadata project with Git, using commits to inspect changes and maintain a clear project history.
  • Used branches and GitHub pull requests, resolved merge conflicts and configured .gitignore to exclude generated outputs.

View my practice repository

docs.title: 11. AI-assisted programming
docs.text:
• Used Ollama and GitHub Copilot CLI to explain, generate and debug small bioinformatics scripts.
  • Wrote focused prompts, reviewed proposed changes and tested translation, reverse-complement and GC-content code against independently checked examples.

docs.title: 12. COVID-19 dashboard — group project
docs.text:
• Collaborated on an interactive COVID-19 dashboard during a 24-hour hackathon, retrieving UKHSA data through an API and organising JSON responses into pandas DataFrames.
  • Combined Matplotlib visualisations, ipywidgets controls and Voilà dashboard presentation, developing collaborative debugging and technical communication skills.

docs.title: Unix and Analysis of Large Genomic Datasets
Introduction and overview
docs.text:
Analysed short- and long-read sequencing data from fire ants and Plasmodium falciparum, developing practical skills in Linux, bioinformatics and genomic data interpretation.

The practicals followed the workflow from read cleaning and assembly to gene annotation, variant discovery and population genetics, alongside genomic and cancer database exercises.

docs.title: Skills developed
docs.text:
• Linux and Bash: Built scripting skills by organising projects and automating repeated steps across samples.
  • Sequencing analysis: Developed quality-control and assembly skills by cleaning reads and evaluating reconstructed sequences.
  • Gene annotation: Assessed predicted gene models through sequence similarity searches and comparison with reference proteins.
  • Variant interpretation: Evaluated SNPs and structural variants using alignment evidence, filtering and genomic context.
  • R and population genetics: Applied visualisation and comparative analysis to genotype data using R-based workflows.
  • Database research: Investigated gene and cancer datasets while considering reference versions, transcript differences and cohort context.
  • Reproducibility and troubleshooting: Managed Conda environments, recorded commands and software versions, and resolved dependency issues.

docs.title: 1. Unix and read quality control
docs.text:
• Worked on remote Linux systems, organised project files and recorded commands in analysis logs.
  • Assessed read quality with FastQC and cleaned paired-end Illumina reads with Trimmomatic, KMC and Cutadapt.

docs.title: 2. Genome assembly
docs.text: • Assembled cleaned reads using SPAdes and evaluated assembly length, GC content and contiguity with QUAST.

docs.title: 3. Gene prediction and annotation
docs.text: • Predicted genes with MAKER and Augustus, and assessed protein predictions using BLASTP, UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot and GeneValidator.

docs.title: 4. Read mapping and variant calling
docs.text:
• Aligned reads with Bowtie2, processed alignment files with SAMtools, and called and filtered SNPs with BCFtools.
  • Inspected alignments and variants in IGV to evaluate read support and potential artefacts.

docs.title: 5. Population genetics
docs.text: • Used R Markdown, adegenet and PopGenome to visualise genetic variation and compare population structure, diversity and differentiation.

docs.title: 6. Long-read analysis on the teaching cluster
docs.text:
• Processed Oxford Nanopore reads using NanoPlot and Chopper, and mapped them to a reference with minimap2.
  • Identified candidate structural variants with Sniffles and used Bash scripts to apply analysis steps across samples.

docs.title: 7. Genomic databases
docs.text: • Queried NCBI, RefSeq, CCDS and UCSC to investigate gene locations, transcripts, annotations and reference assemblies.

docs.title: 8. Cancer genomics databases
docs.text: • Used COSMIC and cBioPortal to study cancer mutation profiles, transcript isoforms, mutation hotspots and copy-number variation.
